To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Confucianism is still very influential, especially in Greater China and the Overseas Chinese Diaspora, but that it is not the only influence on HRM.

(i) the Confucian tradition still influences the degree to which Chinese organizations adopt HRM; (ii) there is a clear difference in the degree to which the tradition influences the practice of HRM in different Chinese contexts, with Hong Kong and Taiwan showing the most adoption of HRM, and the PRC the least; (iii) there are some differences in the degree to the extent to which Confucianism influences HRM in the different Chinese contexts, and (iv) there
the Confucian HR philosophy is still alive and well but in a modern, Westernized form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how far Confucian values are still observable in the practice of HRM, and how this may vary in different parts of Greater China.
the question: to what extent does the Confucian heritage continue to influence the practice of HRM in Greater China and elsewhere?
how far traditional Chinese Confucianism continues to shape the practice of people management in contemporary China.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Confucian HR practices have been adopted in the Greater China region and beyond.
there is no such thing as ‘Confucius HRM’ as such, but there are some elements of Confucian values which are still observable in contemporary HRM practices in Greater China and the Nanyang Diaspora.
there is still a significant degree of Confucian influence on people management in Greater China.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Confucian HR practices can be found in the Greater China region, but not necessarily in all its forms and not necessarily as an all-pervasive influence.
there are three main types of HRM practice: (1) the ‘Confucian’ type, (2) the ‘modern’ type and (3) the ‘mixed’ type.
there is a ‘Confucian HRM’, but one that is not monolithic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no clear boundaries to what we might conceptualize as ‘Confucius HRM’ in Greater China, but rather a spectrum of values that have been adopted and adapted to the local context.
Confucian values still continue to have a significant impact on the way in which people management is practised in the region.
the Chinese culture still has a strong impact on people management in contemporary China, and this is also the case in other Chinese communities around the world.
